title: Selvage Session Protocol — `selvage/2`'s session layer
description: The shapes `selvage/2`'s session layer states that `selvage/1`'s do not: the `GET /meta` body its server advertises, the peer record its replies carry, and the two replies to `session.hello`. Valid against PROTOCOL.md §2, §5 and §6.1. A member `selvage/1` gives a frame and this version does not carry is not a member of it, so the four objects here are what a `selvage/2` producer writes; a receiver tolerates one it is handed anyway (PROTOCOL.md §4.1), so nothing here forbids a member, and what holds a *server* to the member set of its version is the corpus's exact comparison and not this file. `session.hello`'s params are not repeated here: `role` is optional in `methods.json` and its absence is already that schema, so the version's handshake needs no second shape. No vector reaches this file yet — the transcripts are `selvage/1`'s until the corpus is re-baselined — which is why `validate.py` exercises it against values that must and must not validate.

meta.title: `GET /meta`, as a `selvage/2` server answers it
meta.description: The four members `PROTOCOL.md` §2 defines for this version. `/meta` is not a session frame and carries no `v`, so nothing in the body says which version it is about: what tells a client is `wire_versions`, and the members are named again here rather than reused from `meta.json` because JSON Schema has no way to subtract a member from another schema's `required` list. Each member's own schema is `meta.json`'s; only the requirement is per version. `roles` is absent because a `selvage/2` server seats nobody as anything (§1.2) — not forbidden, because `/meta` tolerates a member a reader does not know.

capabilities.description: `["y-protocols/1", "awareness"]` from a server of this version. The other two names `selvage/1` defined are that version's server machinery (PROTOCOL.md §2, §10).

keepalive.description: Unchanged in shape and in membership. In this version `awareness_renew_ms` and `awareness_expire_ms` are the session's only clock, and `room_grace_ms` is how long a room survives its last connection ending (PROTOCOL.md §1.2, §2).

server.description: Free-form server identification, as in `meta.json`: for diagnostics only, and not stable.

wire_versions.description: Names `selvage/2` and no version below it: a `selvage/2` server cannot seat a `selvage/1` peer, and a list offering one would be a downgrade a compromised server could take a client down (PROTOCOL.md §2, §10).

peer.title: `PeerInfo`, in `selvage/2`
peer.description: The record `room.created`, `room.joined` and `peer.joined` carry for a participant. It is `common.json`'s `peer` without `role`: the server seats nobody as anything (PROTOCOL.md §1.2), and the roles a room has are the host's to assign and sign, in the sealed room state (`sealed.json#/$defs/roomState`, PROTOCOL.md §7.1). `role` is not forbidden here — a record carrying one is a record a receiver ignores the member of — and what stops a `selvage/2` server authoring one is the corpus's exact member comparison.

awareness_client_id.description: Omitted when the connection did not claim one, as in `selvage/1`.

roomReply.title: the members `room.created` and `room.joined` share in `selvage/2`
roomReply.description: The reply to a `session.hello` of this version, less the one member that tells a mint from a join. `documents` is not a member of either reply: this version has no server-held open-document set, and no frame says which documents are open (PROTOCOL.md §6.1). The listing, the roles and the host's identity are not here either — they are the host's sealed room state, which arrives over the relay after this frame.

capabilities.description: The same advertised list as `/meta`'s, as in `selvage/1`.

peers.description: The peers already seated, excluding `self`. A set: no order is promised and a receiver must not depend on one.

roomJoined.title: `room.joined`, in `selvage/2`
roomJoined.description: The reply to a `session.hello` that joined a room. It never carries `token`, not even to the connection that minted the room's keys: the token is echoed exactly once, in `room.created` (PROTOCOL.md §5.1, §6.1).

roomCreated.title: `room.created`, in `selvage/2`
roomCreated.description: The reply to a `session.hello` that minted a room. The minting connection is the room's host by holding the private half of the host keypair whose public half the invite's fragment carries — nothing on the server says so — and it is told the token here and nowhere else (PROTOCOL.md §5.1, §6.1).

token.description: Present only here: a client that may have to reconnect has to keep it, since nothing re-sends it.
